description: Analysis window definitions used by feature construction, rule evaluation, and dashboard trends.

notes: Every window ends at the as_of instant and is exclusive of it, which is what keeps feature computation point-in-time correct.
Half-open bounds mean adjacent windows tile the timeline without counting a transaction twice.
Naive timestamps are interpreted as UTC, never as deployment local time, so results do not change with server placement.

comparison_pairs.name: velocity_ratio_7d_30d
comparison_pairs.interpretation: A value well above 0.233 (7/30) means activity is concentrated in the recent week.

comparison_pairs.name: week_over_week
comparison_pairs.interpretation: Compares the last seven days against the seven days before them.

notes: max_lookback_days bounds how far a point-in-time replay may reach, so a backfill cannot scan the whole table.
max_trend_buckets bounds dashboard responses; a wide range is downsampled to a coarser granularity instead of returning thousands of points.
Granularity is chosen from the requested span so a response never exceeds max_trend_buckets.
An account is treated as dormant when it had no completed transfers for 90 days before the window.
Night hours are evaluated in UTC in this prototype.
A production deployment should evaluate them in the account holder's local timezone; doing so in UTC mislabels legitimate daytime activity in some regions.
